ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, and $AB=AC$. Point $P$ is on arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$, and $\angle BAC=30^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle APC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB=AC$, $\angle BAC=30^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle ABC=\angle ACB= \frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-\angle BAC\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-30^\circ\right)=75^\circ$,\\
since quadrilateral ABCP is a cyclic quadrilateral,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC+\angle APC=180^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle APC=180^\circ-\angle ABC=180^\circ-75^\circ=\boxed{105^\circ}$,

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: What is drawn in the figure is a circle, point A is above the circle, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, P is on arc AC on the right side of the circle, and the center of the circle is labeled O. AB, AC, BC as well as AP, PC are connected, so A, B, C, P are all on the same circle. Then reason: It is known that AB=AC, so △ABC is an isosceles triangle, and ∠BAC=30°. Therefore the base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°−30°)/2=75°. Also because the four points A, B, C, P are concyclic, quadrilateral ABCP is a cyclic quadrilateral, and opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠ABC+∠APC=180°. Thus ∠APC=180°−75°=105°.
